rmt-2016-team-01.title: Sum over side lengths
rmt-2016-team-01.body:
A square of side $l$ ($1\le l\le100$) has $101-l$ choices for its left $x$-coordinate and $101-l$ for its bottom $y$-coordinate. The total is $\sum_{l=1}^{100}(101-l)^2=\sum_{j=1}^{100}j^2=\frac{100\cdot101\cdot201}6=338350$.

**Answer: 338350**

rmt-2016-team-02.title: Coordinates
rmt-2016-team-02.body:
Put $A=(0,0)$, $B=(1,0)$, $C=\left(0,\frac43\right)$, $D=(0,1)$. $BD=\sqrt2$, so $E=B+\frac1{\sqrt2}(D-B)=\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt2},\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)$. The line through $E$ parallel to $AB$ meets $AC$ at $F=\left(0,\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)$ and $G=\left(1,\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)$. The flag is the trapezoid $ABEF$ together with triangle $CFG$.

Trapezoid $ABEF$: parallel sides $AB=1$ and $FE=1-\frac1{\sqrt2}$, height $\frac1{\sqrt2}$: area $\frac12\cdot\frac1{\sqrt2}\left(2-\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)=\frac1{\sqrt2}-\frac14$.

Triangle $CFG$: base $FG=1$, height $CF=\frac43-\frac1{\sqrt2}$: area $\frac23-\frac1{2\sqrt2}$.

Total: $\frac23-\frac14+\frac1{\sqrt2}-\frac1{2\sqrt2}=\frac5{12}+\frac1{2\sqrt2}=\frac{5+3\sqrt2}{12}$.

**Answer: $\frac{5+3\sqrt2}{12}$**

rmt-2016-team-03.title: Complementary counting
rmt-2016-team-03.body:
Without the restriction, stars and bars gives $\binom{17+6}{6}=\binom{23}6=100947$ ways. Steven receives more than half exactly when he gets at least $9$ apples; give him $9$ and distribute the other $8$ freely: $\binom{8+6}6=\binom{14}6=3003$ ways. The answer is $100947-3003=97944$.

**Answer: 97944**

rmt-2016-team-04.title: Self-similarity
rmt-2016-team-04.body:
Suppose a high-five happens at time $t_j=x$; since Tal walks at speed $1$, he is at distance $x$ from the origin. Michael runs back to the origin, arriving at time $x+\frac xn$, and then chases Tal. At time $t$ Michael is at $n\left(t-x-\frac xn\right)$ and Tal is at $t$. They meet when $nt-nx-x=t$, i.e. $t_{j+1}=\frac{n+1}{n-1}x$. So $t_{j+1}=\frac{n+1}{n-1}t_j$ for every $j$, and the ratio is constantly $\frac{n+1}{n-1}$.

**Answer: $\frac{n+1}{n-1}$**

rmt-2016-team-05.title: Telescoping sums
rmt-2016-team-05.body:
The sum of changes is $\sum(i+j)-\sum(m+n)$, the sum of initial coordinate sums minus the sum of final coordinate sums. There are $48$ seats and $47$ students; one seat is empty before and one after. If $e_0$ and $e_1$ are the coordinate sums of the empty seats before and after, then the sum of changes is $(S-e_0)-(S-e_1)=e_1-e_0$ where $S$ is the total over all $48$ seats. This is largest when the initially empty seat is $(1,1)$ and the finally empty seat is $(6,8)$: $(6+8)-(1+1)=12$.

**Answer: 12**

rmt-2016-team-06.title: Envelope
rmt-2016-team-06.body:
The segment with parameter $a$ is $\left(\frac\pi2-a\right)x+ay=a\left(\frac\pi2-a\right)$. For fixed $x$ the highest point of $A$ is the maximum over $a$ of $y=\frac\pi2-a-\frac{\pi x}{2a}+x$ (on the segment with $x\le a$). Setting the derivative in $a$ to zero: $-1+\frac{\pi x}{2a^2}=0$, $a=\sqrt{\frac{\pi x}2}$. Then $y=x-2\sqrt{\frac{\pi x}2}+\frac\pi2=\left(\sqrt{\frac\pi2}-\sqrt x\right)^2$, the envelope $\sqrt x+\sqrt y=\sqrt{\frac\pi2}$. $A$ is the region under this curve. With $L=\frac\pi2$: $\int_0^{L}\left(x-2\sqrt{Lx}+L\right)dx=\frac{L^2}2-\frac43L^2+L^2=\frac{L^2}6=\frac{\pi^2}{24}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\pi^2}{24}$**

rmt-2016-team-07.title: Mod 7
rmt-2016-team-07.body:
$6\equiv-1$ and $8\equiv1\pmod7$, so $6^n+8^n\equiv(-1)^n+1$, which is $0$ exactly when $n$ is odd. The smallest odd $n>2015$ is $2017$.

**Answer: 2017**

rmt-2016-team-09.title: Annulus
rmt-2016-team-09.body:
Write $k_1=m_1$, $k_2=(4-2i)+m_2$, $k_3=(3+8i)+m_3$ with $|m_1|=1$, $|m_2|=2$, $|m_3|=4$. Then $\frac{k_1+k_2+k_3}3=\left(\frac73+2i\right)+\frac{m_1+m_2+m_3}3$. The set of values of $m_1+m_2+m_3$ is rotationally symmetric; its modulus ranges over all values from $4-2-1=1$ to $1+2+4=7$ (the triangle inequality, with equality attained, and continuity). So $\frac{m_1+m_2+m_3}3$ fills the annulus $\frac13\le|w|\le\frac73$, with area $\pi\left(\frac{49}9-\frac19\right)=\frac{16\pi}3$ (a translation of the annulus does not change the area).

**Answer: $\frac{16\pi}3$**

rmt-2016-team-10.title: Semicircle argument
rmt-2016-team-10.body:
The triangle is obtuse (or right) exactly when the three points lie on a common semicircle. Fix the first point; the probability that all three lie on a semicircle is $3\cdot\frac14=\frac34$ (for each point $P_i$, the probability that the other two lie in the half-circle going clockwise from $P_i$ is $\frac14$, and these events are disjoint). So the probability of an acute triangle is $1-\frac34=\frac14$.

(Alternatively: the three arcs between the points are uniformly distributed on a simplex, and the triangle is acute iff all arcs are less than a semicircle; the probability that no arc exceeds half of the circle is $1-3\cdot\frac14=\frac14$.)

**Answer: $\frac14$**

rmt-2016-team-11.title: Stars and bars
rmt-2016-team-11.body:
An $n$-digit ascending number has all digits in $\{1,\dots,9\}$ (a $0$ would be a leading digit), in nondecreasing order, so $a_n=\binom{n+8}8$. A descending sequence of $n$ digits from $\{0,\dots,9\}$ is determined by the multiset, giving $\binom{n+9}9$, minus the all-zero sequence which is not an $n$-digit positive integer: $b_n=\binom{n+9}9-1$. Then $\frac{b_n}{a_n}=\frac{n+9}9-\frac1{\binom{n+8}8}=\frac n9+1-\frac1{\binom{n+8}8}$, and $\frac1{\binom{n+8}8}\to0$. So $\frac{b_n}{a_n}-xn-y\to0$ iff $x=\frac19$, $y=1$.

**Answer: $\left(\frac19,1\right)$**

rmt-2016-team-12.title: Tangent iteration
rmt-2016-team-12.body:
Since $\frac{2x}{1-x^2}=\tan(2\arctan x)$, the $n$-th iterate of $g(x)=\frac{2x}{1-x^2}$ is $\tan(2^n\arctan x)$. The "half iterate" is $f(x)=\tan\left(\sqrt2\arctan x\right)$, which satisfies $f(f(x))=\tan(2\arctan x)$ and is discontinuous exactly where $\sqrt2\arctan x=\pm\frac\pi2$ (two points). Then $f(\sqrt3)=\tan\left(\sqrt2\cdot\frac\pi3\right)=\tan\frac{\sqrt2\pi}3\approx11.10$.

**Answer: $\tan\dfrac{\sqrt2\,\pi}3$**

rmt-2016-team-13.title: Partial fractions
rmt-2016-team-13.body:
$\frac1{(k+m)(k-m)}=\frac1{2m}\left(\frac1{k-m}-\frac1{k+m}\right)$. Split the sum into $k<m$ and $k>m$. For $k=1,\dots,m-1$: $\sum\left(\frac1{k-m}-\frac1{k+m}\right)=-\sum_{n=1}^{m-1}\frac1n-\sum_{j=m+1}^{2m-1}\frac1j$. For $k>m$, with $n=k-m$: $\sum_{n=1}^\infty\left(\frac1n-\frac1{n+2m}\right)=\sum_{n=1}^{2m}\frac1n$ (telescoping). Adding, everything cancels except the terms $\frac1m$ and $\frac1{2m}$ of the harmonic sum: the total is $\frac1m+\frac1{2m}=\frac3{2m}$. Multiplying by $\frac1{2m}$ gives $\frac3{4m^2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{3}{4m^2}$**

rmt-2016-team-14.title: Reduce to one parameter
rmt-2016-team-14.body:
Shifting $a$ and $b$ by the same amount shifts $x$, so we may assume $b=0$, and since $\{x+a\}$ depends only on $a$ modulo $1$, $0\le a<1$. The function $\{x+a\}+2\{x\}$ is piecewise linear with slope $3$ and jumps down at $x\equiv-a$ and $x\equiv0\pmod1$. Its suprema are approached just before these jumps: just before $x=1-a$ the value tends to $1+2(1-a)=3-2a$, and just before $x=1$ it tends to $a+2=2+a$. So $M_{a,0}=\max(3-2a,\,2+a)$. The first is decreasing and the second increasing in $a$; they are equal at $a=\frac13$, where the maximum is minimized: $M=\frac73$.

**Answer: $\frac73$**

rmt-2016-team-15.title: Tangency condition
rmt-2016-team-15.body:
Substituting $y^2=1-(x-1)^2=2x-x^2$ into the ellipse equation gives $b^2x^2+a^2(2x-x^2)=a^2b^2$, i.e. $(b^2-a^2)x^2+2a^2x-a^2b^2=0$. Tangency at two points (symmetric above and below the axis) means this quadratic has a double root: $(2a^2)^2+4(b^2-a^2)a^2b^2=0$, i.e. $a^2b^4-a^4b^2+a^4=0$, so $b^2=\frac{a^2-\sqrt{a^4-4a^2}}2$ (the root with $b<a$; this needs $a^2\ge4$). The area is $\pi ab$, so minimize $a^2b^2=\frac{a^4-a^3\sqrt{a^2-4}}2$. Setting the derivative to zero gives $a^3\sqrt{a^2-4}=a^4-3a^2$, i.e. $a^6(a^2-4)=a^8-6a^6+9a^4$, which simplifies to $a^4(2a^2-9)=0$, so $a^2=\frac92$. Then $b^2=\frac{\frac92-\sqrt{\frac{81}4-18}}2=\frac{\frac92-\frac32}2=\frac32$. Hence $(a,b)=\left(\frac{3\sqrt2}2,\frac{\sqrt6}2\right)$.

**Answer: $\left(\frac{3\sqrt2}2,\frac{\sqrt6}2\right)$**
